script.text: A giant AI model now runs on two desktop Macs. Why does that matter?

Meta released Muse Spark Open on October fifteenth. It is an open-weight model, so anyone can download its trained settings. Meta says it has eight hundred sixteen billion parameters, with forty-two billion active at a time.

Apple and Meta say it runs locally across two Mac Studio computers with M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX software. Reports put the memory need at one terabyte. So no cloud server is required, but that is far beyond a normal laptop. Apple also published new benchmarks for its chips, CNBC reports.
Meta calls it the most capable U.S. open-weight model to date. That is Meta's own claim, not independently verified. According to CNBC, the license allows only limited commercial use.
Will most people run AI on their own devices soon? Yes or no?
